overview: A one-page Department of State list of papers for file 894A.156 indexes two reports concerning Japanese harbor development and maritime strategy: a June 1938 report from Joseph C. Grew on the significance of Takao, Formosa, to Japan’s “Southward Advance” policy, with material derived from the Italian naval attaché in Tokyo; and an October 1939 report from John K. Emmerson on the establishment and ceremonial naming of a new port at Gosei in Taiwan’s Taichung region.

people.name: Joseph C. Grew

people.name: John K. Emmerson
people.role: U.S. Foreign Service officer at Taihoku; identified as the author of report no. 81

subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers for File 894A.156
subfiles.about: An index records two papers concerning the strategic significance and development of harbors in Japanese-ruled Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: The first entry describes Joseph C. Grew’s telegram of June 22, 1938, concerning Takao’s importance to Japan’s “Southward Advance” policy and notes an enclosed naval attaché report translating information sent from Tokyo to the Italian Admiralty. The second entry describes John K. Emmerson’s October 2, 1939, report on a new port at Gosei in Taichung Prefecture, ceremonially named “Miitaka” on September 25 by the governor-general. The underlying telegram, report, and enclosure are indexed but are not reproduced on this page.

interest: This index is useful for connecting Taiwan’s colonial harbor construction with Japan’s broader southward strategic ambitions immediately before the Pacific War. It also points to an unusual intelligence chain in which an Italian naval attaché’s report from Tokyo was translated and enclosed in an American diplomatic communication. The second entry helps document the official creation and naming of the modern Port of Taichung, although the OCR forms “Taishu” and “Miitaka” likely represent Taichū and Niitaka.
